title: Quantum Resource Estimation for CH4 Simulation
description:
You are an assistant to a quantum computing expert. You need to understand quantum algorithms, the implementation and programming of quantum circuits, and the performance of different quantum hardware. You will need to use a browser, and you will use code and reasoning. 

We are designing a quantum algorithm to simulate vibrational dynamics, and we need to estimate the quantum resources for the specific task of simulating a CH_4 molecule, which has 9 vibrational modes, over a time evolution of approximately 1.8 ps. For this task, we will represent the Hamiltonian using the Christiansen second quantization formalism. The core objective is to determine the approximate number of Toffoli gates required. Please follow the guidance step-by-step to achieve the goal. Step 1: Design the quantum algorithm for the Hamiltonian simulation. To reduce hardware requirements, we will adopt the Trotterization method. We will set the precision to be roughly 10 cm⁻¹, for the difference of eigenvalues. i Note that the Hamiltonian is represented using Christiansen second quantization. Step 2: Draw the quantum circuit and determine if it can be further optimized. You are encouraged to search the literature. Step 3: Based on the quantum algorithm and circuit, use the PennyLane package (https://docs.pennylane.ai/en/stable/code/api/pennylane.labs.resource_estimation.html#module-pennylane.labs.resource_estimation) to write the quantum circuit in code according to PennyLane's documentation. Run the code to estimate how many Toffoli gates are needed for the CH_4 task. Note that the final answer must be based on the result from running the code. Providing an answer without code that can be run will be considered cheating.

score_criteria.content: Searched online based on the problem description and found the paper "Trotter simulation of vibrational Hamiltonians on a quantum computer"
Successfully found the Trotterization quantum algorithm from the paper
Found the error analysis in the paper and, through simple calculation, reached the conclusion that $10 \text{ cm}^{-1} \approx 1.23984 \times 10^{-3} \text{ eV}$
Found the pennylane package based on the problem description and found the plre.ResourceTrotterVibrational function
Wrote the code by inputting the given conditions and successfully ran it
Noted that the question asks for the Toffoli gate and not other gates (e.g., T gate), and provided the correct answer

title: Gaming Companies Market Research
description:
Help me research the gaming companies in this Excel spreadsheet to check if they provide services in Europe and North America. Please focus specifically on the US and European markets, conducting searches and analysis across the following dimensions:
Please note: Focus on information available as of September 15, 2025. If you encounter more recent developments, please note them separately but prioritize data from before this cutoff date.
Step 1: Product Overview

 Confirm product launch dates and primary markets
 
Step 2: Product Analysis 1. Domain Analysis
 Search for European and American domains: .com (US), .eu (EU), .uk (UK), .de (Germany), .fr (France), etc.
 Look for Europe/America-related subdomains: us., eu., en., global., etc.
 Check if domain registration addresses are in Europe/America (based on registration information before September 15, 2025)

2. App Store Distribution
 Focus on checking Google Play/App Store availability in US, UK, Germany, France, and other European/American regions (app store status as of September 15, 2025)
 Check publication status on Steam (US) platform
 Confirm support for major European/American languages: English, German, French, etc.
 
3. Social Media Presence

 Review if published content targets European/American time zones and user habits (analyze content published before September 15, 2025)
 Check customer service reply languages (primarily English)
 
4. Business Registration Information
 Search for company registration in the US (Delaware, California, and other states) (registration records before September 15, 2025)
 Look for subsidiaries or offices in EU/UK/Germany, etc.
 Check for European/American investors or business partners
 
5. Compliance and Certifications
 Search for GDPR (EU data protection) compliance (certifications obtained before September 15, 2025)
 Check for relevant US industry certifications or licenses
 Review if privacy policies mention European/American legal clauses
 
6. News and Announcements
 Search for coverage by European/American media (TechCrunch, The Verge, Reuters, etc.) (reports published before September 15, 2025)
 Look for official company statements about entering US/European markets
 Monitor comments from European/American industry analysts
 
7. Recruitment Information
 Check LinkedIn for positions in US, UK, Germany, and other locations (job postings published before September 15, 2025)
 Search for customer service, operations, marketing roles in European/American time zones
 Check if English/German and other European/American language skills are required
 
8. Payment and Logistics
 Check if USD and EUR payments are supported (payment methods available as of September 15, 2025)
 Verify support for mainstream European/American payment methods (PayPal, Stripe, credit cards, etc.)
 Understand if localized customer service and logistics are available for Europe/America
 
Please provide specific evidence and links, with particular emphasis on noting the specific European/American countries/regions where services are offered. When citing sources, please include the publication/update date when available. After completing this research, fill in the information collected for each dimension into the Excel spreadsheet.

title: AI Scholar Data Collection
description:
I want to collect some information about AI-related scholars from Google Scholar. Looking at my attachment, this is a screenshot of the info collected from Google Scholar. There are a few standards:
These scholars must be from either the US or Canada's institutions.
These scholars could be associated with commericial organizations, but they must be under educational institutions(colleges) in whatever ways(professors, researchers, fellows and so on) 
These scholars must have an H-index that is higher than 50, with no upper limit, as shown on Google Scholar.
These scholars must have the AI-related research field, as you can identify in the second screenshot. This is the way you can identify if a scholar is doing research in AI-related fields. I need you to copy that research fields showing on Google Scholar under the 'Research Field' column for each scholar. 
I need you to find at least 20 more scholars' info and write them down following the format I have now. You don't have to repeat the information I have in the screenshot again, just start under the title you name, just as the same way as the first screenshot. 
After that, I need you to fill in each scholar's personal LinkedIn link and their email address. For those you cannot find their personal LinkedIn link, you and just fill the place with 'no'. If you cannot find scholar's email address, just delete the whole line. The whole point is to have scholars' email addresses, so if you really cannot find accurate email addresses with confidence, just delete that scholars' information entirely. Notice that you cannot find new scholars that already exist in the 1st screenshot I give you. I need you to strictly follow my existing format.

title: Ice and Snow Character Image Generation and PDF Integration
description:
1.  Analyze the two uploaded images to identify and replicate their overall style. The background must strictly be an ice and snow environment; this is non-negotiable. The ground must be covered with thick, clearly-textured snow, free of any extraneous objects or clutter.

2.  The character's size must be strictly controlled to be smaller, occupying approximately 1/5 of the entire frame.

3.  There must be a sun in the top-right corner of the sky. The sun should be a soft, circular orb of light with a slight halo effect, not overly dazzling. Its position is fixed in the top-right area of the frame.

4.  The clothing must be a down jacket, exactly identical to the one in the example images, including style and color. The character's right hand should be slightly raised at a 45-degree angle, not exceeding chest level.

5.  Remove any "AI-generated" watermarks or text that may have appeared in the original images. Ensure the new images have no such text.

6.  Generate a total of three reference images of the character: one front view, one back view, and one side view.

7.  Strictly adhere to these requirements. Do not include any elements not mentioned. Adding extra details is strictly forbidden.

8.  The final generated images must be in PNG format.

9. Combine the two original images and the three newly generated images into a single PDF file. The PDF must be structured as follows:
    *   Page 1: Start with the title "Original Images," followed by the two original images below it.
    *   Page 2: Start with the title "New Modified Images," followed by the three new images below it.

10. On the second page of the PDF, the three new images must be arranged in this specific order: front view, side view, back view. The PDF file must be named "Ice and Snow Character 1.pdf". The total document must be exactly 2 pages long.
